summary: Cossack officer Reza Khan seized power in Persia in a British-backed 1921 coup, crowned himself Reza Shah Pahlavi and ruled Iran as a brutal autocrat until the Allies forced him to abdicate in 1941.

evidence.note: Qajar dynasty's 1785 rise and Fath Ali Shah begin the narrative of the secondary subject
Reza Khan born March 1878 in Alasht, Mazandaran
February 1921 march on Tehran with Cossacks starts the coup
Allied invasion forces abdication in 1941; dies in Johannesburg 1944
oil company segregates and sidelines Persian workers, imports Indian labour
Persianization campaign and massacre of Lurs under his rule
British Admiralty decision in London to switch navy to Persian oil
Tsar's Cossacks and Russian influence shape the Persian brigade
explicit account of beheadings and cauterized necks
WWI armies fight over neutral Persia, seize food and housing; famine follows
Curzon's Anglo-Persian Treaty, bribes and its defeat in the Majlis
Russian Civil War spills into Persia: Soviet republic in the north vs Whites, British, Cossacks
